heading: What an update keeps
body:
When a service value changes, the browser renderer renders the view again. It keeps every element that is still at the same place in the template and has the same loop item. It changes only the attributes, text and children that are different. So the element keeps its DOM node, its focus, its caret and its scroll position. In the example, a click on a card changes `graph.selected`. The scrolling `div` and the three buttons stay the same nodes, so the view does not jump back to the start.

A loop item keeps its element when it is the same object, or a plain object or array with the same values. So a list that a getter or a method builds again on every render keeps its elements, the focus, the caret and an open native `<select>` inside them. A loop item whose values changed gets a new element. A `<select>` shows the option that its `:value` or its options' `:selected` choose after every update, also when the options come from a loop and change. A `<select>` without either keeps the option that the user chose. A custom element, for example one from a component library, stays only when its children and its light-DOM `slot` elements are as the renderer left them. If the library moved them, or an attribute that the element observes changes, the renderer creates the element again. When the focus was inside it, the new element gets the focus and the same selection.
